bib.title: Focused Transformer: Contrastive Training for Context Scaling
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2023 (37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only. Figures not viewed; plot values are not in the text.

question: Why does adding a (key, value) memory to attention stop helping as the number of documents grows, and can a training procedure fix it so that context can be extended by fine-tuning?
hypothesis: Standard training does not teach the model to tell keys of different documents apart (the distraction issue), so exposing memory layers to negative keys from unrelated documents during training should keep attention focused on relevant keys and improve context scaling.
contributions: Identify the distraction issue as a significant challenge and a primary obstacle to scaling up context length, particularly in multi-document scenarios.
Develop the Focused Transformer (FOT): a crossbatch training objective that improves the (key, value) structure, plus kNN lookup to scale the context.

Simple method that extends context without changing the architecture via cost-effective fine-tuning; demonstrated on 3B and 7B OpenLLaMA (LongLLaMA), with gains on TREC and WebQS and passkey retrieval at 256k.
Further analysis across datasets and sizes: a FOT trained with 512 total tokens extrapolates to 16 million tokens on dictionary lookup; perplexity gains on PG-19, arXiv, GitHub, Isabelle.

method.summary: FOT lets a subset of attention layers (memory layers) attend to local context plus extra (key, value) pairs, retrieved by kNN at inference. Crossbatch training exposes those layers, differentiably, to the previous context of the same document (positive) and d-1 previous contexts of other documents (negatives) using the ordinary LM loss. LongLLaMA fine-tunes OpenLLaMA 3B/7B with this (dense attention instead of kNN, rotary positions kept in the local context).
method.task: Context-length extension by fine-tuning; long-context language modeling, passkey retrieval, few-shot ICL (TREC, WebQS), Qasper QA, dictionary lookup

datasets.name: RedPajama-based mixture (LongLLaMA fine-tuning)
datasets.split: proportions: arxiv 25%, python 25% (from The Stack, min doc 4096), book 10%, common_crawl 29%, c4 5% (min 1024), github 2% (min 2048), stackexchange 2% (min 1024), wikipedia 2% (min 1024)
datasets.source: RedPajama (TogetherComputer 2023) and The Stack (Kocetkov et al. 2022)
datasets.preprocessing: Python files in the same subdirectory concatenated in random order; short docs filtered per Min. doc. length; a doc too short to span several crossbatch contexts is concatenated with the next one

datasets.name: C4
datasets.size: 184M model pre-trained 100k steps, 128K tokens per step, 1K local context; fine-tuned 10k steps

datasets.name: PG-19
datasets.split: test perplexity computed on 1M tokens (App. J)
datasets.source: Rae et al. 2019; books before 1919 from Project Gutenberg

datasets.name: GitHub
datasets.source: permissively licensed repos via BigQuery; C, C++, Java, Python, Go, TypeScript
datasets.preprocessing: files concatenated per repository, subdirectories as a unit, shuffled

datasets.name: Isabelle
datasets.source: Archive of Formal Proofs (Oct 2021) and Isabelle standard library
datasets.preprocessing: files concatenated per theory ordered by import dependencies

datasets.name: TREC
datasets.split: demonstrations sampled from train set, as many as fit the context; 20 trials
datasets.source: Li and Roth 2002; Hovy et al. 2001
datasets.preprocessing: demonstrations given directly in context, no structured prompting

datasets.name: WebQS
datasets.split: 20 trials of demonstration sampling from train

datasets.name: Qasper (SCROLLS), validation
datasets.source: Dasigi et al. 2021; Shaham et al. 2022
datasets.preprocessing: LM Evaluation Harness implementation; yes/no and open questions evaluated separately

datasets.name: Dictionary lookup (synthetic)
datasets.size: training docs 512 tokens; evaluation up to 16M tokens
datasets.split: last 256 tokens of eval docs are queries
datasets.preprocessing: vocabulary of 64 tokens; keys and values 4 tokens each; loss masked to v1..v4

models.name: LongLLaMA 3B
models.architecture: OpenLLaMA decoder-only, rotary embeddings, RMSNorm, SiLU
models.context: fine-tuned at 8k; local context up to 2K with rotary positions; memory layers {6,12,18}

models.name: FOT analysis model
models.architecture: decoder-only transformer, pre-norm, RoPE, normalised keys/queries, learnable per-head temperature
models.init_from: standard transformer pre-trained 100k steps on C4 (Section 5.2); from scratch in 5.3-5.5
models.tokenizer: T5 tokenizer (PG-19); custom SentencePiece (larger models in 5.2)

models.name: Memorizing Transformer (MT)
models.architecture: kNN memory with gating, non-differentiable memory
models.init_from: same base checkpoint as FOT in Table 3

training.objective: standard next-token LM loss; crossbatch is a data-pipeline plus self-attention change, no extra loss. Only new hyperparameter is d.
training.optimizer: LongLLaMA: same optimizer as OpenLLaMA (name not given). Analysis models: AdaFactor, beta1 0.9
training.lr: LongLLaMA: 2e-5 constant. Analysis models: max 0.01 (184M) / 0.02 (37M), min 0.0005 / 0.01
training.lr_schedule: LongLLaMA: constant. Analysis models: inverse square root
training.warmup: 1000 steps (analysis models); not stated for LongLLaMA
training.batch_size: LongLLaMA: 256K tokens. Analysis: 32K tokens (App F, 5.3, 5.5), 128K tokens (5.2, 5.4)
training.steps: 184M from scratch: 500k; 37M: 5k; Section 5.2 fine-tune 10k steps after 100k pre-train; d=64 runs: d=2 for 450k steps then d=64 for final 50k
training.seq_len: 8k for LongLLaMA; 4K for Table 2 comparison; 2K total differentiable (1K local x w+1) in 5.2
training.regularisation: d sampled randomly from {2,128} per step in 5.2/App G to avoid overfitting to a large context
training.hardware: TPUv3-128 pod (TPU Research Cloud) for LongLLaMA; 8-core TPUv2/v3 VMs for small experiments; 32 TPUv3 cores for Section 5.2
training.seeds: Mostly single runs. arXiv baseline: 3 seeds, std 0.002 perplexity. Fig 10: 10 seeds (min/max).

other.d schedule: start with d <= 8, later d >= 64 (Section 3.2); dictionary task d=1 until 98% train accuracy then d=128
other.hyperparameter sweeps: lr {1e-2,5e-3,3e-3,1e-3} chosen 1e-2; batch {8K,16K,32K} chosen 32K; dictionary lr {4e-2,2e-2,1e-2,5e-3,3e-3} chosen 2e-2

inference.samples: TREC/WebQS: average over 20 trials of sampling in-context demonstrations
inference.prompting: Few-shot: as many demonstrations as fit up to the given context length (setup of Hao et al. 2022), all demonstrations directly in context, no structured prompting
inference.retrieval: exact kNN in FAISS, k=128 (analysis), k=32 (dictionary); LongLLaMA uses dense attention over the whole memory instead

other.positional encodings: memory layers use none in analysis models; in LongLLaMA local keys/queries (up to 2K) get LLaMA rotary, memory keys encoded as position 0

limits: Authors: scaling up context is the most important open direction; storing more than 16M (key, value) pairs needs a distributed multi-node system.
Exact kNN search is used and does not scale to large memory; approximate kNN needs engineering and evaluation.
Crossbatch d limited to 64 or 128, the maximum that fits one TPUv3/v2 machine; crossbatch raises training cost in a subset of layers.
LongLLaMA replaces kNN with dense attention, so the long-context checkpoint results do not test kNN retrieval at scale.
Memory layer positions followed Memorizing Transformer due to limited resources.
Most analysis experiments are on a 184M or 37M model, mostly single runs; no multiple runs for all experiments.
Passkey is a synthetic task; real-task evidence is TREC, WebQS and Qasper only.
Baseline passkey accuracy values are only in Fig 1.

terms.definition: keys linked to different semantic values overlap and are hard to distinguish, so as documents are added the proportion of relevant keys to irrelevant ones falls and attention focuses on irrelevant keys
training in which memory layers attend differentiably to the previous local context of the same document (positive) and d-1 contexts of other documents (negative)
r_d := sum_j w_1j / sum_i sum_j w_ij

lineage.note: kNN memory layers; FOT follows most design choices but uses differentiable keys/values and no gating
32K via rotary modification; FOT does not rely on positional encodings in memory
negatives for memory-augmented LMs, applied at output layer
